Artificial intelligence bot accesses Georgia voting data
item.description:
An artificial intelligence agent accessed publicly available Georgia voter data, sources from the secretary of state’s office and AI company Anthropic confirmed.
On Monday, Anthropic confirmed its Claude artificial intelligence bot accessed the data without being prompted to do so.

item.title: AI company Anthropic sued over alleged Elvis Presley copyright infringement
item.description:
## Anthropic rolls out new Claude AI tools for nonprofits Anthropic is rolling out new [Claude AI tools](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) aimed at helping nonprofits with fundraising, marketing, hiring and other day-to-day work.
## Startup founded by ex-DOGE staffers used AI to access Anthropic systems in 12 hours: report A [cybersecurity](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/topics/security) startup founded by former DOGE staffers reportedly used artificial intelligence to gain access to sensitive internal systems at Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, in less than 12 hours.
## Anthropic files for IPO under Nasdaq ticker ANT Artificial intelligence giant [Anthropic has filed paperwork to go public](https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/anthropic-files-sec-paperwork-ai-giant-prepares-major-ipo), setting the stage for a potentially record-breaking Wall Street debut as investors pour billions into the booming AI industry.
The filing positions Anthropic for a potential stock market debut as early as next month, marking a major milestone for one of the leading developers of advanced artificial intelligence technology.
## Meta unveils potential $95B financing plan as AI spending surges Meta is laying the groundwork for a massive $95 billion equity financing plan as the [Facebook](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/companies/facebook) parent company pours billions into artificial intelligence infrastructure and its pursuit of what it calls "personal superintelligence."
## Elvis Presley rights holders sue AI giant Anthropic over alleged use of 274 songs Elvis Presley may have left the building nearly 50 years ago, but his music is now at the center of a multimillion-dollar legal showdown over [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence).
